name: IllumiNeuro Protocol

card.summary: A vendor-sold four-peptide nootropic blend marketed for memory, focus and stress resilience, aimed at sharper mental performance.
card.note: Research-labeled product; no clinical studies of the combination and contents vary by seller.

quick.overview:
IllumiNeuro Protocol is a research-peptide blend sold by vendors as a nootropic. One database lists its contents as PE-22-28, Pinealon, NA-Semax Amidate and NA-Selank Amidate in a single vial [1].

It is marketed for memory, focus, learning, stress resilience and mood support, typically by subcutaneous injection and sometimes intranasally [1].
quick.mechanism: The blend combines peptides associated with different roles: Semax-type peptides for focus and memory, Selank-type for stress and anxiety, and others listed for neuroprotection and circadian support [1].
quick.risks: The listing says it is not approved for human use and that no clinical studies exist on this four-peptide combination [1]. Listed side effects include injection-site reactions, nasal irritation, vivid dreams and headache; listed cautions include bipolar disorder, psychosis, pregnancy and seizure disorders, and batch variability is noted [1].

chain: Marketed for memory, focus and calm
angle.text: Users take blends like this hoping for better focus and lower stress, which people tie to sleep, mood and a more energetic presence.

lead: IllumiNeuro Protocol is a multi-peptide nootropic blend sold by research-peptide vendors [1]. One database lists per-vial components as PE-22-28, Pinealon, NA-Semax Amidate and NA-Selank Amidate, though other sellers describe different vial contents and amounts [1].

Vendors market it for memory, focus, learning, neuroprotection, anxiety reduction, mood support and circadian support, mostly by subcutaneous injection, with intranasal use also mentioned [1]. The listing labels research as limited and states that no clinical studies exist on the combination [1].
infobox: PE-22-28, Pinealon, NA-Semax Amidate, NA-Selank Amidate [1]

paras: No studies found. The database listing states that no clinical studies exist on this specific four-peptide combination and that human efficacy data for the individual peptides are limited [1].

Listed side effects are mild injection-site reactions, nasal irritation, vivid dreams and initial headache; listed contraindications include bipolar disorder or psychosis, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and seizure disorders as a theoretical concern. The listing also notes possible batch variability and recommends certificates of analysis [1].
